output.narrative_summary: This result rests on the link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin. If throughput assumptions shift, more runs could support a different option. In this model, 53% of runs supported Move to Four Day Week, and the options are close.

story_headlines.opt_four_day: Move to Four Day Week holds on modelled throughput and retention gains lifting Operating Margin.
story_headlines.opt_status_quo: Keep Current Schedule would gain support if Delivery Throughput proves stronger than currently modelled.

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 56% of variations, based on current estimates given the moderate confidence behind it.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin is the single biggest threat to this result.
stability_factors: Staff Retention's link to Operating Margin is comparatively well evidenced
fragility_factors: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin could flip which option more runs support

output.readiness_rationale: The comparison is close and a single relationship, Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin, is not yet settled enough to act on with confidence.

fac_throughput.specific_action: Pull recent delivery throughput data from your project tracking tool and compare against pre-change baselines.

flip_thresholds.narrative: If Delivery Throughput moves from 44% to 49%, more runs would support a different option.

key_assumptions: The link from Delivery Throughput to Operating Margin assumes current working patterns translate directly into margin impact
The link from Staff Retention to Operating Margin assumes retention gains persist beyond an initial adjustment period
